title: `-0.0` in arithmetic: two zeros
description: Arithmetic keeps the sign of zero: `1.0 / -0.0` is -inf, `-(0.0)` and `0.0 * -1` are -0.0, `sqrt(-0.0)` is -0.0. Comparison, grouping and sorting are in polars-zero-order.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: The same section at tag py-2.1.0.

provenance.notes: Polars's user guide says it generally follows IEEE 754 for `Float32` and `Float64`, with two exceptions: any NaN equals any other NaN and is greater than every non-NaN value, and operations guarantee nothing about the sign of zero or NaN or a NaN's payload (a sort or group by may make every zero +0 and every NaN a positive NaN). It promises no error bound unless a function says otherwise. The user guide is not versioned; the section reads the same at tag py-2.1.0. So the two zeros the probes show are what Polars 2.1.0 happens to do: the docs do not promise them, and a sort or group by may turn `-0.0` into `0.0`. The `Float32` rows stay open.
